 committed head 4ebd12e8d (the sha run 37868446568 actually tested) produces exactly one match, in a docstring at fallback_snapshot.py:123 — so 
 every ``FalkorProjection(":memory:")`` in one CWD... — and the file contains **no** FalkorProjection construction at all.                      
 tools/redis-guard.py:63-65 scans line-by-line with no docstring awareness, so it read ":memory:" as a relative path. One prose line cascades   
 into redis-guard → test-carve-out (b) (test_whole_repo_clean, the only failure: 1 failed, 472 passed) → python-ci-gate.                        
                                                                                                                                                
 Two things follow. Worth more than the fix: this PR carries a signed verdict=clean review record at that exact head (PR-body line 49) while a  
 required check at that head was red — a review reads code and cannot see a guard, so "review recorded at the head" and "the head is landable"  
 are independent facts. And the guard pushes authors the wrong way: the flagged sentence documents why the code keys on the store instance; the 
 holder's one-word reflow takes the file 1 match → 0 and leaves the guard unable to tell prose from code for the next author. That is the       
 workaround #5268 explicitly rejects, so I reported there (6073039542) as a second instance of the same root — different guard, same mechanism  
 — rather than filing a peer, and told #7786's holder not to reach for # noqa (6073041520).
